title: Allah Made the Mosquito
pages: The garden around {childName}'s house was full of life. Big creatures, small creatures, and some so tiny you could hardly see them.
{childName} noticed almost all of them. But one day, {m:he|f:she} nearly stepped right on a line of ants.
One day a friend came running over, and the two of them raced around the meadow until evening.
Suddenly, something whined right next to {m:his|f:her} ear. {childName} froze, one hand in the air.
The mosquito kept buzzing, but {childName}'s hand just hung there. It didn't swat. {m:He|f:She} wasn't even sure why.
{m:His|f:Her} friend didn't stop, though. Smack! A slap at the ear, and a miss. The mosquito flew off, and the friend shook out a stinging hand.
"Ugh, mosquitoes! Why do they even exist?!" the friend groaned.
{childName} shrugged and promised to ask Mom about it that evening.
At dinner, {childName} asked, "Mom, what are mosquitoes for?"
Mom smiled and nodded toward Grandpa's room.
Grandpa was sitting in his armchair by the lamp, reading the Qur'an.
"Grandpa, what are mosquitoes for?" {childName} stood in the doorway, looking very serious.
Grandpa burst out laughing. He laughed so hard that {childName} didn't know what to say.
"Let's ask the Qur'an," said Grandpa, and he opened the Book to just the right page.
"Truly, Allah is not shy to give an example, even of a mosquito..." Grandpa read aloud.
{childName} waited for more, but Grandpa closed the Qur'an and smiled.
"That's it?" {childName} was a little disappointed. {m:He'd|f:She'd} hoped for a clearer answer.
"Allah mentioned the mosquito in the Qur'an because it matters. The rest, you can figure out yourself."
{childName} thought hard. {m:He|f:She} sat down, then lay back on the rug and stared at the ceiling.
"Grandpa, do you know the answer?" Grandpa laughed again, and {childName} could tell: he did.
"Swallows catch mosquitoes right out of the air. Quick as a flash."
"At night, bats hunt them. One flap of the wings, and the mosquito's gone."
"Dragonflies, fish, and frogs eat mosquitoes too."
"Without mosquitoes, all of them would go hungry." Grandpa looked over at {childName}.
"Ohhh..." {childName} said slowly, nodding. Now it all made sense.
"And did you know that boy mosquitoes don't bite?" Grandpa added.
{childName} squinted. Was Grandpa joking?
"They drink nectar from flowers, just like bees. And they help the flowers bloom."
"A mosquito lands on a flower, and pollen sticks to its legs. Then it flies to the next flower and takes the pollen along."
"Scientists studied the mosquito's long, thin mouth. It gave them the idea for super-thin needles."
{childName} rubbed {m:his|f:her} arm, right where shots usually go, and took another look at the picture.
"And that whining sound by your ear, do you know what it is?" asked Grandpa. {childName} shrugged.
"It's the sound of its wings. A mosquito flaps them six hundred times a second."
"Six hundred!" {childName} started flapping {m:his|f:her} arms as fast as {m:he|f:she} could.
"Wow," {childName} whispered. "The wonders of Allah," Grandpa whispered back.
The next day, {childName} found {m:his|f:her} friend in the same meadow.
"Remember how you asked why we even need mosquitoes?"
"Yeah, so?" the friend said with a shrug. "It's not that interesting."
{childName} told the whole story: the swallows, the fish, the needles, the six hundred flaps a second. The friend was only half listening.
But little by little, the friend got curious and leaned in closer.
"Six hundred times a second?" "Yep." {childName} nodded, just like Grandpa.
The friend didn't say anything, just gazed out over the meadow, thinking.
A mosquito flew past. They both watched it go.
The friend started to raise a hand, then changed {m:his|f:her} mind right away.
